title: Canada CPI inflation, May 2026
question: Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index, all-items, Canada, 12-month percent change for May 2026, not seasonally adjusted, first print
resolutionSource: Statistics Canada The Daily Consumer Price Index release and Table 18-10-0004-01
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first Statistics Canada print for the May 2026 all-items Consumer Price Index 12-month change for Canada, not seasonally adjusted, as published in The Daily and sourced to Table 18-10-0004-01. Use the published one-decimal percent value; ignore later revisions or table updates after the first official May release.
drivers: April headline inflation was 2.8 percent after 2.4 percent in March and 1.8 percent in February
April energy and gasoline effects remained large, with energy up 19.2 percent year over year and gasoline up 28.6 percent
May comparison should lose some April-specific carbon-levy base pressure but retain elevated fuel-price risk
Full-month effect of the temporary federal fuel excise tax suspension should partly offset higher crude and gasoline pressure
Core and ex-gasoline readings in April were materially lower than headline, with CPI excluding gasoline at 2.0 percent

reasoning.text: Forecast Canada all-items CPI year-over-year inflation for May 2026
The resolver is the first Statistics Canada May 2026 all-items CPI 12-month change for Canada, not seasonally adjusted, published in The Daily and Table 18-10-0004-01 to one decimal percent.

reasoning.call: Checked Statistics Canada The Daily Consumer Price Index, April 2026 release.
reasoning.result: Fetched April 2026 all-items CPI 12-month change 2.8%, March prior 2.4%, month-over-month CPI 0.4%, seasonally adjusted monthly 0.3%, CPI excluding gasoline 2.0%, energy 19.2%, gasoline 28.6%, fuel oil and other fuels 41.3%.

reasoning.call: Checked Statistics Canada The Daily Consumer Price Index, March 2026 release.
reasoning.result: Fetched March 2026 all-items CPI 12-month change 2.4%, February prior 1.8%, month-over-month CPI 0.9%, seasonally adjusted monthly 0.5%, energy 3.9%, gasoline 5.9%, gasoline monthly 21.2%, food from stores 4.4%.

reasoning.call: Checked Statistics Canada The Daily Consumer Price Index, February 2026 release.
reasoning.result: Fetched February 2026 all-items CPI 12-month change 1.8%, January prior 2.3%, month-over-month CPI 0.5%, seasonally adjusted monthly 0.1%, gasoline -14.2%, natural gas -17.1%, food from stores 4.1%.

reasoning.call: Checked Statistics Canada The Daily Consumer Price Index, January 2026 and December 2025 releases.
reasoning.result: Fetched January 2026 all-items CPI 12-month change 2.3%, December 2025 all-items CPI 12-month change 2.4%, January CPI excluding food and energy 2.4%, January CPI excluding gasoline 3.0%, December gasoline -13.8%.

reasoning.call: Checked official release timing in the April 2026 CPI Daily note.
reasoning.result: Fetched official next-release timing: May CPI will be released on Monday, June 22, 2026; basket weights table update date June 15, 2026; May release uses updated basket weights one week later.

reasoning.text: Base-rate reference class: the last five headline prints were 2.4, 2.3, 1.8, 2.4, and 2.8 percent, averaging 2.34 percent, while the latest three-month average was about 2.33 percent. The near-term trend and energy shock argue above that base, but not far above April because April already incorporated a large gasoline and carbon-levy base effect.

Counter-consideration: if Middle East-linked oil prices or local gasoline prices rose further through May, the print could exceed 3 percent; if the full-month fuel excise tax suspension and softer shelter or travel components dominated, May could fall toward the low 2s.

Anchor on April 2.8. Add about +0.1 for continued energy pass-through and recent upward momentum, subtract about -0.2 for April-specific base effects and a full month of fuel-tax relief, giving 2.7. Use an 80% interval of 2.1 to 3.4 to cover typical one-month CPI surprise plus unusually high gasoline volatility.
